mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the lustre of metals is NOT true?

options.A: Metals appear shiny because they reflect most of the incident light.
options.B: The lustre of a metal can be reduced if its surface gets oxidized.
options.C: All metals have the same degree of lustre.
options.D: Polishing a metal surface restores its lustre.

mcqs.answer: All metals have the same degree of lustre.
mcqs.explanation: Option C is incorrect because different metals exhibit different degrees of lustre; for example, gold has a distinct yellow shine while iron appears silvery. Options A, B and D are true statements about metallic lustre, making C the only false choice. This clarifies the misconception that all metals are equally shiny.

mcqs.question: A student hammers a piece of metal into a thin sheet without it breaking. Which property is being demonstrated?
mcqs.explanation: Malleability is the ability of a metal to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets without cracking. The described action directly tests this property. Ductility (option A) refers to drawing into wires, hardness (C) is resistance to deformation, and brittleness (D) is the tendency to fracture—none of which describe the observed behaviour.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches the metal with the property it best exhibits?

options.A: Copper can be drawn into wires easily, showing high ductility, while lead can be hammered into sheets easily, showing high malleability.
options.B: Iron can be drawn into wires easily, showing high ductility, while gold can be hammered into sheets easily, showing high malleability.
options.C: Lead can be drawn into wires easily, showing high ductility, while copper can be hammered into sheets easily, showing high malleability.
options.D: Gold can be drawn into wires easily, showing high ductility, while iron can be hammered into sheets easily, showing high malleability.

mcqs.answer: Copper can be drawn into wires easily, showing high ductility, while lead can be hammered into sheets easily, showing high malleability.
mcqs.explanation: Copper is well‑known for its excellent ductility, allowing it to be drawn into thin wires. Lead, on the other hand, is soft and can be easily hammered into thin sheets, demonstrating high malleability. Options B, C and D mismatch the typical properties of the listed metals, making A the correct comparison.

mcqs.question: Why are metals good conductors of electricity?

options.A: Metals have a crystalline lattice with free electrons that can move under an electric field.
options.B: Metals have tightly bound electrons that cannot move, allowing current flow.
options.C: Metals contain positively charged ions that carry the current.
options.D: Metals have high resistivity due to electron scattering.

mcqs.answer: Metals have a crystalline lattice with free electrons that can move under an electric field.
mcqs.explanation: In metallic bonding, valence electrons are delocalised and form a ‘sea of free electrons’ throughout the crystal lattice. These electrons can drift when an electric field is applied, producing electric current. Options B and D describe the opposite of metallic behaviour, and option C incorrectly attributes conductivity to ions rather than electrons. Hence, A correctly explains metallic conductivity.
